newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-BOETSCH UPSETS ENQVIST, MEETS KAFELNIKOV IN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BOETSCH UPSETS ENQVIST, MEETS KAFELNIKOV IN FINAL.

text.p: Arnaud Boetsch sent France's Davis Cup final opponents Sweden a warning when he came from behind to beat fifth seed Thomas Enqvist and reach the final of the Lyon Grand Prix on Saturday.

The unseeded Frenchman meets Russian Yevgeny Kafelnikov in Sunday's final after upsetting Enqvist 4-6 6-4 6-0 in their semifinal, an aperitif to the Davis Cup final between their two countries in Sweden at the end of November.
Earlier, number two seed Kafelnikov crushed Tim Henman 6-1 6-3, avenging his surprise elimination by the Briton in the first round at Wimbledon.

Boetsch, who will play the 10th final of his career, said: "In the light of the Davis Cup, such a victory can only give one confidence. You retain the images of the match and you know you have shaken hands with the guy as a winner.
"It also gives you an idea of his game and what worries him," added the Frenchman, who made a crucial break of service in the third game of the second set.
With a devastating third set in which he did not drop a game, Boetsch wound up the match in an hour and 50 minutes.
Enqvist said: "I served badly today, while Arnaud served very well. Indoors, it (service) is the main weapon, so it was logical he should win."
Boetsch beat Kafelnikov in their only previous encounter at Essen last year.
"It's going to be tough. Kafelnikov has improved immensely since the Essen match. He's won Roland Garros, he has a lot of shots, he's a completely different player," Boetsch said.

The Russian world number five, who took just 58 minutes to dispose of Henman, said: "So many things were said after Wimbledon that I wanted to show there is a difference between top 10 players and the rest."
